rationale: The docs job runs `uv sync --group docs` on every push and pull request, repeatedly downloading the same pinned docs dependencies (Sphinx and plugins) even though uv.lock and pyproject.toml change infrequently. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-download-cache pattern applies: repeated dependency fetching is measurable (ci_history shows repeated runs) and cache inputs can include the lockfile (uv.lock and pyproject.toml are present in the repository). Adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/uv, keyed on uv.lock and pyproject.toml with a restore-key prefix, reuses downloaded packages across runs. This preserves the Sphinx build, site assembly, and required-check/deploy coverage exactly, adds no secrets or privileged actions, and does not add new network access (it reduces pip/uv downloads). Measured corroboration: the batch-hiruni experiment recorded about 9.2% elapsed savings from adding the same actions/cache@v4 dependency-cache step.
